sections.note: This coast has no station-by-station entries: these family paragraphs are the only telling of the station returns. Entries are by FAMILY ('Turdidæ.--', 'Sylviinæ.--', ... 'Alcidæ.--'), not by species. Spring and autumn share one paragraph: the 'Spring:' part comes first and the autumn part starts mid-line with '--Autumn:' (e.g. line 309). Several families hold more than one species, run on without a break, each starting mid-line as 'Name.--Spring:' or 'Name.--Autumn:'. For example Anatidæ: 'Swans.--Spring:' 558, 'Eider Ducks.--Spring:' 566, 'Sheldrake.--Autumn:' 576, 'Teal.--' 582. Charadriadæ: 'Oystercatcher.--' 603, 'Lapwing.--' 607, 'Ringed Plover.--' 612. Scolopacidæ: 'Woodcock.--' 620, 'Snipe.--' 623, '"Sandpipers."--' 629. Laridæ: 'Iceland Gull.--' 650, 'Storm Petrels.--' 653. Stations are named in prose, with no markup and no numbers (except 'station 27', 'station 26' at 289-290). The Turdidæ entry carries a long note on the Isle of May rush of Sept. 22nd (287-303), which later entries refer back to. Records from other sources sit inside entries: Lerwick/Dumfries 416-420, Loch Leven 584-588, Aberuthven 594-597, 'Field' 518. Lines 403-405 are in square brackets. The Alcidæ paragraph turns mid-line at 671 ('Besides the 75 identified species, or thereby,') into Isle of May records of unidentified birds (to 692). Line 287 prints 'Bell Pock' for Bell Rock.

notes: The whole file (1-4575) is covered in 33 consecutive sections, with no gaps or overlaps. The coast headings are at lines 130, 703, 1806, 2396 and 3192. Neither Scottish coast has entries by station or by date: their observations are only the family paragraphs (279-693 and 1888-2213), so those are marked primary. Both English coasts have species reports under 'SEPARATE REPORT ON EACH SPECIES.' (776, 2512). Ireland is autumn only: an introduction, a station table, a table of entry dates, keepers' remarks by station, then a day-by-day diary. The diary stops at Dec. 15th, although the date table and the title promise entries to January 1882. There are keepers' names in all five station lists except Ireland's; Irish keepers are named at the end of each entry in 'General Remarks of Light-Keepers' (3417-3667). The West Coast of England list (2433-2494) also prints light characters and heights for several stations. Misprints worth knowing: 'North Uist' for North Unst (183), 'Kirk Bank' for Kish (3323), 'Howth Daily' (3703), and 'Bushes'/'Pushes' for Rushes in the West Coast of Scotland families.
